note that this improvement has broken apps using [webpack-subresource-integrity](https://github.com/waysact/webpack-subresource-integrity), since the contenthash in filename doesn't change, but the actual content has changed. @jscheid 
If the old file has been cached on CDN or user browsers, the sri integrity hash won't match with the cached file.
This sounds like a bug in the contenthash, which it doesn't actually use real final output file content.

If your analysis is correct @zlk89 then it's breaking any app using SRI and long-term caching (regardless of whether it's using our plugin or some other way to add SRI) so there's little we can do about it...
@jscheid you are right, it actually is a bug on filename generation on webpack side.
@zlk89 I can't reproduce that. Did you disable `optimization.realContentHash`?
Please create a repro repo and file a new issue
Just created a repro repo, looks like it is related with the SRI plugin actually https://github.com/waysact/webpack-subresource-integrity/issues/152 @sokra

@zlk89 if I read the description in https://github.com/waysact/webpack-subresource-integrity/issues/152 correctly, you can get different files with the same name, depending on which webpack version you use.

This means that if you use SRI with long-term caching things will break for users who previously loaded one version of the asset and now are loading the other.

The reason is that the SRI hash will have changed, but the file contents will not have changed from the browser's perspective, because it will reuse the old cached value.

In short, SRI will break if you use long-term (content-independent) caching and your file contents change without their names changing. Or, more generally: it will break if a changed file isn't refreshed for some reason, but the file that contains the (changed) SRI hashes _is_ refreshed.

This is not a limitation in our plugin -- it's a fundamental problem with SRI and caching.

But perhaps I'm missing something?

@jscheid I just updated the description a little bit. So the problem here is: when SRI plugin is used, webpack cannot calculate contenthash correctly, when content is changed. 
As long as I remove the SRI plugin, webpack DOES generate different contenthash filenames for them.
Ah, ok, that's different then. I'll take a look. @sokra off the top of your head, any idea why this might happen?
Ah, scratch that, it _is_ returning a different value in some cases, that must be what's causing it.

No, wait -- it should just be updating SRI values inside assets, it shouldn't have any effect on the final filename hash except indirectly through the hash updates -- but those updates shouldn't negate the effect of the JSON syntax changes?
Ah I see. You must not return the oldHash from updateHash. Return undefined when you don't want to customize the hash update.
Ah! Right. Could you update the bindings to allow undefined as a return value? https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/3849f45961c60d4bea91b4ef43bb7da7992a0c3a/types.d.ts#L1676

issue_context.title: json module type inline using single-quotes
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please don't delete this template or we'll close your issue -->

## Feature request

I noticed that when the JSON is inlined as a double-quoted string, which then requires all double-quotes inside the string to be backslash-escaped. I think this can be improved by using a single-quote string.

For example, this is what I'm seeing in the output for one of my projects:

```javascript
JSON.parse("{\"の\":{\"seq\":\"no\",\"weight\":1918313},\"に\":{\"seq\":\"ni\",\"weight\":1108840},\"た\": ... ");
```

**What is the expected behavior?**

The current behaviour is fine. It seems not to be ideal.

It could probably be something like:

```javascript
JSON.parse('{"の":{"seq":"no","weight":1918313},"に":{"seq":"ni","weight":1108840},"た": ... ');
```

**What is motivation or use case for adding/changing the behavior?**

This will decrease the size of the output since the doublequotes around the JSON object keys will no longer be backslash-escaped.

**How should this be implemented in your opinion?**

Emit the `JSON.parse` argument as a single-quoted string by changing [line 167 of JsonGenerator.js](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/blob/4ab27ff7234ac37f11d29c5e3790c05fd33bfda6/lib/json/JsonGenerator.js#L167) to be:
```javascript
`JSON.parse('${jsonStr}')`
```

instead of:

```javascript
`JSON.parse(${JSON.stringify(jsonStr)})`
```

I'm fairly certain that this change should be well supported on any JS engine (but I'm not _100%_ sure).

**Are you willing to work on this yourself?**

Yes!

review_comments: newlines should also be escaped as they would break the single quoted string into multiple lines making it invalid.
though stringifySafe does not permit newlines, so that would not happen - but then test is needed to ensure it is not regressed in the future.
since this is the output of `JSON.stringify` it won't contain newlines and most other weird stuff is already escaped.
We have tests with new lines in JSON, so I guess this should already be covered
